question: A 74-year-old man presents malnourished with multiple bruises at different healing stages. He appears fearful when his son (who accompanies him) speaks. Which of the following actions is MOST appropriate as the attending physician?

answers.text: Discharge the patient immediately as this is a family matter

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Discharging without assessment or action would put the patient at continued risk. Elder abuse is a medical and safeguarding concern.

answers.text: Interview the patient privately, document findings, and refer to the hospital social worker

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Suspected elder abuse requires private patient interview (without the possible abuser present), thorough documentation, and referral to social work and — if indicated — the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007 authorities or police.

answers.text: Confront the son directly about the bruises in the patient's presence

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Confronting the suspected abuser in front of the patient may escalate the situation and can place the patient in immediate danger.

answers.text: Reassure the patient that bruising is normal in elderly patients and discharge

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Multiple bruises at different healing stages in a fearful elderly patient are a red flag for physical abuse and must not be dismissed as normal ageing.

overallFeedback.feedback: Elder abuse protocol: private interview (separate from suspected abuser), document injuries carefully, refer to social work, and consider the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007 as legal recourse.
Correct. Private interview, documentation, and social work/legal referral are the correct steps for suspected elder abuse under Indian law and clinical safeguarding guidelines.
